_comment: OPS-CLOSEDBAR-RECALIBRATE-READINESS-W1 — the readiness gate for OPS-CLOSEDBAR-RECALIBRATE-W{NEXT}. Every threshold lives HERE with a `reason`, never in the script body, so the recalibration wave inherits a declared instrument rather than a number someone remembered. Derived at Step 0 from MEASURED accrual (2026-08-07, 3.19h post-boundary: 874 emitted / 410 matured) and from the outcome backfill's OWN maturity horizon (EVAL_CANDLES in src/lib/pfe-mae.ts) — deliberately NOT inherited from the shadow window, whose n>=500 floor answered a different question.

methodology_boundary.reason: SIGNAL-CLOSEDBAR-FLIP-W1 recorded the flip as an INTERVAL, not an instant: the engine flipped at 10:16:12Z but the mandatory >=2h measurement window sat between it and the bot/seeder changes at 12:25:23Z / 12:28:57Z. Signals emitted INSIDE the interval carry mixed methodology and are excluded from every post-flip statistic. Re-read from status.md at runtime; this copy is the fallback and the drift check.

matured_total.reason: MEASURED 410 matured in 3.19h post-boundary, dominated by the fast timeframes. 5000 is roughly two days of total accrual. Deliberately NOT the binding term — it exists to catch a stalled backfill, which is the real failure mode; the coarse timeframes gate readiness long before this does.

distinct_utc_days.reason: 1d's maturity horizon is 72h (EVAL_CANDLES 1d=3 candles), so no 1d outcome matures at all before day 3. 7 days yields ~4 days of MATURED 1d data rather than a single point. This is the term that actually sets the calendar date.

per_venue_matured.reason: Slowest promoted venue observed ~1.5 matured/h post-boundary (PHEMEX 5 in 3.19h), so 30 lands in ~20h — never the binding term. Its job is to make a venue-BLIND report impossible to pass, which is the F2 defect the flip's Step 0 had to reconstruct by hand (the shadow report carried no venue breakdown at all, and the spec's 87.8% floor rate was a Binance/XRP proxy against a real 78.58%, spanning 2.85%-78.58% across venues).

per_timeframe_matured._reason: A single global M would be set by the slowest EMITTER and would over-gate every fast timeframe for no benefit. Floors are scaled to measured emission rate, not to maturity: maturity is fast everywhere (1d is only 72h), but 1d emits ~3/day against 5m's ~92/h.

3m.reason: measured 44.5 emitted/h, 98.6% matured at 36min horizon — reaches 100 within hours

5m.reason: measured 92 emitted/h, 91.8% matured at 1h horizon — the fastest accruing timeframe

4h.reason: measured 5.6 emitted/h, 24h horizon — ~2 days; halved because emission is an order of magnitude below the fast timeframes

8h.reason: measured 0.31 emitted/h, 32h horizon — ~3 days at 10. A higher floor would push readiness past two weeks for no analytical gain

1d.reason: THE BINDING TERM. ~3 emitted/day and a 72h horizon, so 10 matured 1d outcomes takes ~6-7 days — which is what sets distinct_utc_days=7. Raising this to 30 would push readiness to ~2 weeks.

atom_detection.reason: A candidate threshold is REJECTED when any single |raw| value within +/-6 of it holds more than 3x the mean count of that neighbourhood. MEASURED atoms this must reject: raw=41 carries ~10,748 rows and raw=-55 carries ~12,873 (|raw|>54 admits 13,152 vs |raw|>55 admits 281 — a 47x cliff). The score space is discrete (fixed indicator ladders x fixed weights), so thresholds land ON mass points routinely; CLAUDE.md forced this rule after the flip, and here it becomes executable rather than remembered.

accrual_stall.reason: A silently-stalled outcome backfill would hold the verdict at NOT_READY forever with no explanation — the failure mode that looks identical to 'not enough data yet'. 48h is well past the slowest maturity horizon (1d = 72h emits continuously, so matured counts should never be flat for two days).

ready.reason: Fires ONCE ever. A readiness gate that re-announces itself every hour trains the operator to mute it.

stalled.reason: Distinct id and distinct wave from the readiness alert — one recommended_wave shared by two alerts with opposite remedies is the generator bug that sent an operator to run the wave that would have ratified a broken state.
